chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), he said: I heard him saying:

'Three kinds of people have their supplications returned to them unanswered. One of them is a man who prays against his wife while he is unjust to her, and it is said to him: Did We not place her affair in your hand?'

key_terms.أَمْرَهَا بِيَدِكَ: Her affair/authority over her is in your hand — i.e., the husband has the right of divorce
key_terms.تُرَدُّ دَعْوَتُهُمْ: The supplication/prayer is rejected and returned unanswered
key_terms.ظَالِمٌ: One who is unjust, an oppressor; here the husband who wrongs his wife

ai.seo_question: What types of prayer are rejected according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) relates, through al-Walid ibn Sabih, that three categories of people will have their prayers rejected and returned unanswered. One such person is a man who supplicates against his wife while he himself is the one oppressing her. In this case, God responds rhetorically: since He gave the husband the authority to divorce her, the husband cannot complain about the very power he was entrusted with. This teaching reflects the jurisprudential principle that the husband's authority in marriage comes with corresponding responsibility — abuse of this power nullifies the moral standing of his complaints.

en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from al-Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

The prayers of three kinds of people are returned to them without a favorable answer. One of such people is one who prays against his wife to whom he is unjust and it is said to him, ‘Have we not given you the authority to divorce her?”’
